steps.title: Your First I2C Device
steps.markdownContent:
### Inspecting the 16x2 Character LCD (`comp_07`)
A standard 16-character by 2-line liquid crystal display has 16 raw header pins. Wiring it in parallel requires dozens of wires and consumes almost all Arduino I/O pins.

Our `comp_07` display features an onboard black daughterboard: the **PCF8574 I2C Backpack**. The backpack converts those 16 parallel pins into a streamlined 4-pin I2C interface!

### The 4 Backpack Pins:
1. **GND:** Connect to Arduino Uno **GND** (Black / Slate wire).
2. **VCC:** Connect to Arduino Uno **5V** (Red wire).
3. **SDA:** Connect to Arduino Uno Analog Pin **A4** (Blue wire).
4. **SCL:** Connect to Arduino Uno Analog Pin **A5** (Yellow wire).

```
LCD Backpack [ GND | VCC | SDA | SCL ]
               │     │     │     │
Arduino Uno   [ GND | 5V  | A4  | A5  ]
```

### ⚠️ The Blue Contrast Trimpot Trap
Look at the small blue potentiometer on the back of the I2C backpack. If you power on the screen and see blank boxes or solid black rectangles, do not panic! Use a small screwdriver to gently rotate this trimpot until crisp, clear text appears.

### Hands-On Wiring Steps:
1. **Safety First:** Unplug the USB cable from your Arduino Uno.
2. Connect female-to-male jumper wires to the LCD backpack header pins.
3. Wire `GND` to Uno `GND` and `VCC` to Uno `5V`.
4. Wire `SDA` to Uno `A4` and `SCL` to Uno `A5`.
5. Double check every wire connection before reconnecting USB power!

quickCheck.question: Before plugging jumper wires between your Arduino Uno and the 16x2 I2C LCD backpack, what safe hardware workflow step must you take?
options: Unplug the USB cable from your computer to completely disconnect power.
Press the red reset button for ten seconds while powered on.
Increase the Arduino IDE baud rate to 115200.
quickCheck.explanation: Always disconnect USB power before creating or changing wiring connections on breadboards and breakout modules to prevent short circuits.
quickCheck.warmupExplanation: Remember the fundamental lab rule from Lesson 2A and Lesson 5: never build or wire live circuits!

quickCheck.question: If your I2C LCD powers up with the backlight illuminated but characters do not appear on screen, what hardware adjustment should you check first?
options: The blue contrast potentiometer on the back of the I2C backpack module.
Reverse the 5V and GND wires to invert polarity.
quickCheck.explanation: The blue contrast trimpot on the PCF8574 backpack sets the liquid crystal contrast voltage; if it is turned too far, characters become invisible or all black boxes.
quickCheck.warmupExplanation: In Lesson 6, you learned that potentiometers act as adjustable voltage dividers; the LCD backpack uses a tiny trimpot to tune display contrast.

steps.title: The 16x2 I2C Backpack Architecture
steps.markdownContent:
### Anatomical Tour of the I2C LCD (`comp_07`)

A standard 16x2 LCD display can show 16 characters across 2 rows. On its back sits a black daughterboard: the **PCF8574 I2C Backpack**:

```
+──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────+
|            REAR VIEW: 16x2 CHARACTER LCD BACKPACK        |
|                                                          |
|   [ 16-Pin Header to HD44780 LCD Controller Glass ]      |
|                                                          |
|        [ PCF8574 ]           [ Blue Contrast Pot ]       |
|    8-Bit I2C I/O Expander     Rotate with screwdriver!   |
|                                                          |
|        [ A0 A1 A2 ]          [ 4-Pin Bus Header ]        |
|      Address Jumper Pads       GND  VCC  SDA  SCL        |
+──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────+
```

- **PCF8574 Chip**: An 8-bit remote I/O expander that receives serial commands over I2C and toggles the 16 LCD pins in parallel.
- **Blue Contrast Potentiometer**: Controls liquid crystal alignment voltage. If text is invisible or all white boxes, this pot needs adjusting!
- **Backlight Jumper**: A physical jumper shunt that powers the LED backlight.

steps.title: Wiring & Contrast Potentiometer Adjustment
steps.markdownContent:
### Hardware Mission: Wiring the 16x2 LCD

**Golden Rule:** Always unplug your Arduino USB cable before connecting wires!

Connect the 4 wires from the backpack header:
1. **GND** -> Arduino Uno **GND** (Black wire)
2. **VCC** -> Arduino Uno **5V** (Red wire)
3. **SDA** -> Arduino Uno **A4** (or dedicated SDA pin)
4. **SCL** -> Arduino Uno **A5** (or dedicated SCL pin)

**The Contrast Potentiometer Trap:**
When first powered, the screen may look blank or show a row of solid rectangles! Use a small Phillips screwdriver to gently rotate the blue contrast pot on the backpack until crisp, clear letters appear.

**Workbench Task:**
Practice diagnosing LCD wiring and contrast issues in the interactive troubleshooting bench below!

interactiveConfig.question: How many total wires are needed to interface a 16x2 LCD backpack with an Arduino Uno?
interactiveConfig.explanation: The I2C backpack collapses the 16 parallel pins down to just 4 wires: power (VCC), ground (GND), serial data (SDA), and serial clock (SCL).

questions.question: How many total wires are needed to interface a 16x2 LCD backpack with an Arduino Uno?
questions.explanation: The I2C backpack collapses the 16 parallel pins down to just 4 wires: power (VCC), ground (GND), serial data (SDA), and serial clock (SCL).

questions.question: If the LCD backlight turns on but no text characters appear on the screen, what is the first hardware adjustment you should check?
options: Gently turn the blue contrast potentiometer on the back of the I2C backpack
Replace the Arduino board with a different model
questions.explanation: If the contrast potentiometer is turned too far in either direction, characters will either be completely washed out or hidden under solid black blocks.
